summary: @servicetitan/carto-react-kit ships an obfuscated preinstall dropper that fetches the Bun runtime to execute a hidden payload
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscator.io-style obfuscated and, at install time, downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against sibling math_init.js via execFileSync. math_init.js is a ~727 KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle carrying obfuscator.io fingerprints (random identifiers, large scrambled string/integer table, string-array-rotation decoder) and is executed under the freshly downloaded alien runtime rather than under Node, so the payload never runs under a Node-visible execution path. The package advertises itself as a React component kit under the `@servicetitan` scope but ships no functionality consistent with that description; the only install-time effect is the runtime-dropper chain. Fetching a second language runtime solely to execute a bundled, obfuscated, purpose-mismatched blob on `npm install` is an alternate-runtime dropper against installers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
